en: use soap faithfully every day.
note: continues #3199 (slice 039), which must end so a lowercase verb follows

en: After all, living as filthy as a beggar is
hardly what you'd call a human life.
You really do like to keep clean.
Thank you as always for your custom.
How nice it would be if everyone
in London kept so clean.
Do come by any time.
I've expanded my stock quite a bit lately.
Oh? And who might you be?
Don't tell me you're a detective?
There've been so many violent crimes lately.
I'm afraid I don't know anything, though.
At any rate, thank you for your hard work.
Oh, so you're not a detective after all?
I jumped to conclusions there. My apologies.
Oh. Sorry, I'm still taking in new stock.
I can't put out goods before checking stock.
The shop will open in a little while.
Hahaha, please wait just a little longer.
Don't worry, the goods won't run away.
Welcome.
Truth is, my home's much like the shop, but
would you like to come in?
Even my home smells of soap and chemicals
now, I'm afraid. I don't mind it, but
some people find it unpleasant.
Do come again whenever you like.
A servant's life knows neither clean
nor unclean... I'll let you live
free of needless worries.
You feel easier now, don't you? Hahaha
Soap? Is it really selling that well?
Hmm, is that so?
In that case, I'll take one.
hardly what you'd call a cultured life.
Even indoors, it smells of soap and chemicals
I shall serve you
I just can't shake this tiredness. It's odd.
I go to bed early, since I have work.
Last night I dreamed I got into a fistfight
with someone in the street at midnight.
It felt awfully real. It scares me.
Welcome! Care for some tea?
Taking tea has really caught on
among Londoners, too.
I've only just arrived in London, so I know
little of such matters...
Taking tea is the fashion, is it?
That's right.
Afternoon tea used to be a pastime
for elegant aristocrats only.
But now that tea leaves have gotten cheaper,
ordinary folk can enjoy their tea
as well. Isn't that wonderful?
Indeed. Then I'll take this one.
Hm, a fine aroma.
Isn't it? That one's very popular.
Thanks to the tea craze, I'm doing well
for myself too. Come again any time.
Hello there! Care for some tea?
I'm glad you came by the shop, too.
I'm proud of my range. Go on, take a look.
Do try our own house blend, too.
Thankfully, my tea's a hit with customers.
Nothing beats a hot cup of tea after work.
If a youngster like me can make his way
like this, it's because I was lucky enough
to catch the trend. I'm truly grateful.
Oops, sorry if that sounded like bragging.
The tea you bought last time must be
running out about now, right?
note: variant for msg 120251, where it is joined on one line after #3311 (slice 041), which is a full clause there

en: Sharp of you, as ever.
Tea isn't bad either. Its aroma is quite fine.
Isn't it? Quite right.
With tea, the aroma is everything.
I take great care over quality, too.
Even a single cup of tea can ease
a weary person's heart, can't it?
I do want to turn a profit, but
